blocks.text: Say: "Our Lord will assemble us all together (on the Day of Resurrection), then He will judge between us with truth. And He is the (Most Trustworthy) All-Knowing Judge."
Our Lord comprehends all things in His Knowledge. In Allah (Alone) we put our trust. Our Lord! Judge between us and our people in truth, for You are the Best of those who give judgment.

The meaning of this Name is the One who rules over His servants with whatever He wishes, He judges between them with what He Wills. He gives those of them He Wills whatever He Wills. Nothing can repel His rule and nothing comes after His decree and command. Allaah the Exalted said,
Whatever of mercy (i.e. of good) Allah may grant to mankind, none can withhold it, and whatever He may withhold, none can grant it thereafter. And He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.

A servant's belief that His Lord is Al-Fattaah The Judge should make him turn to Allaah alone in a good manner to open the doors of guidance for him, the doors of provision, the doors of mercy and that Allaah opens his heart to do good.

Is he whose breast Allah has opened to Islam, so that he is in light from His Lord (as he who is non-Muslim)? So, woe to those whose hearts are hardened against remembrance of Allah! They are in plain error!

This opening/conquest/expanding does not have a limit. Every believer takes a share from it. The Prophets succeeded in taking the highest share, then after them the awliyaa' allies of Allaah, then the scholars, then the general believers and no one will fail except the disbelievers.
blocks.ref: Al Asnaa fee Sharh Asmaa Allaah al Husnaa 1/225

keyPoints: Al-Fattaah is the One who rules over His servants with whatever He wishes and judges between them with what He Wills.
He gives whom He Wills whatever He Wills; nothing can repel His rule and nothing comes after His decree and command.
Believing that Allaah is Al-Fattaah should make the servant turn to Allaah alone to open for him the doors of guidance, provision and mercy, and to open his heart to do good.
Qurtubi said this opening has no limit: every believer takes a share, the Prophets the highest, then the awliyaa', then the scholars, then the general believers; only the disbelievers fail.

evidence.text: Then He will judge between us with truth. And He is the (Most Trustworthy) All-Knowing Judge.
Whatever of mercy Allah may grant to mankind, none can withhold it, and whatever He may withhold, none can grant it thereafter.

recall.q: What does Al-Fattaah (The Just Judge) mean?
recall.a: The One who rules over His servants with whatever He wishes, judges between them with what He Wills and gives whom He Wills whatever He Wills; nothing can repel His rule.

recall.q: What should a servant's belief that his Lord is Al-Fattaah lead him to do?
recall.a: Turn to Allaah alone in a good manner to open for him the doors of guidance, provision and mercy, and to open his heart to do good.

recall.q: Which aayah does the author cite showing that none can withhold what Allaah grants?
recall.a: Faatir 35:2: "Whatever of mercy Allah may grant to mankind, none can withhold it, and whatever He may withhold, none can grant it thereafter."

recall.q: According to Qurtubi, who takes the highest share of Allaah's opening?
recall.a: The Prophets, then the awliyaa', then the scholars, then the general believers; no one fails except the disbelievers.
